verdict.rationale: pnpm's docs show install behavior suited to unattended agents. It automatically switches to frozen-lockfile mode in CI, and it fails installs on stale lockfiles, missing offline packages, or unresolvable workspace versions, which gives deterministic failure on error. However, no evidence explicitly documents exit codes, error formats, or a non-interactive flag for local agent runs, and `pnpm update` appears only in passing. Missing for 10: documented exit codes and structured error output for install/update, an explicit non-interactive or no-prompt mode outside CI detection, hands-on corroboration of agent-driven updates.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent install and update project dependencies non-interactively, with clear exit codes and errors when something fails

citations.quote: When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.
In a CI environment, installation fails if a lockfile is present but needs an update.
If a package won't be found locally, the installation will fail.
Run a full dependency resolution and report what a real install would change, without writing anything to disk.
